concept.name: Three black crows
concept.definition: A three-candlestick top reversal pattern consisting of three consecutive long black candles with progressively lower closes, each closing at or near its low and each opening within the prior candle's real body. Technical analysts read it as steady, sustained selling marking a top after an advance; it is the bearish mirror of three white soldiers.
concept.intuition: Three sessions in a row of relentless selling, each closing near its lows and stepping lower, suggests determined distribution rather than a single day of profit-taking.
concept.mechanics: From OHLC data: three long black bodies with C1 > C2 > C3; each candle opens within the previous body and closes near its low (small lower shadows). Appearing after an uptrend or at resistance, the stepped structure is meant to distinguish sustained selling from a one-day flush.
concept.failure_modes: After three strong down candles the market is often short-term oversold and due for a bounce, so the pattern frequently completes just before a rebound. Shallow or gapped candles that do not meet the stepped structure are weaker and fail more often.
concept.misconceptions: It is not a signal to short aggressively after completion; the move it 'predicts' has often already happened, so practitioners typically wait for a pullback to enter. Candles with long lower shadows (buying support) do not form a textbook three black crows.
concept.example: After a rally to 95.00, a stock prints three consecutive daily candles closing at 93.50, 92.00, and 90.50, each opening inside the prior body and closing near its low. The three black crows are read as evidence of a durable top.
